title: GPU lease vs commitment — HC tradeoff & pricing sensitivity (June 2026)
body:
Summary:
Purpose: rapid comparison of short-term GPU lease/spot + burst contractor labor vs 12/24/36-month GPU commitments and headcount (HC) tradeoffs. Focus: throughput-on-demand economics for Q3–Q4 2026 expected mid-season spike, and price sensitivity thresholds where we should switch from lease-burst strategy to committing or shifting HC weight to SRE/infra hires.

Key assumptions (working):
- Baseline model-mix: 55% generation, 30% embeddings, 15% reranking.
- Avg tokens per gen call: 120.
- Expected Q3 spike profile: +4.5x peak over baseline for 3 rolling weeks in Aug 2026; +2x baseline for remainder of quarter.
- GPU options (per-GPU monthly effective cost incl power/colocation):
    * Lease/spot (short-term): $1,200/mo (includes margin to reseller) — availability variable, contended; used only for bursting.
    * On-demand cloud (per-GPU equivalent): $2,500/mo — high availability, high cost.
    * 12-month Reserved: $1,100/mo effective (commit discount applied).
    * 24-month Reserved: $950/mo effective.
    * 36-month Reserved: $820/mo effective (bigger commitment).
- Contractor infra engineers for burst ops: $120/hr fully-loaded (sourcing via agencies). Internal HC (infra engineer): fully-loaded $34k/mo (~$204k/yr).
- Utilization target: steady-state 60% avg, spike peak target 85% to avoid tail latency violations.
- SLA penalty cost estimate: $45k per month of sustained SLA misses during spike week.

Model of tradeoffs (simplified):
- Option A (Lease + contractors): maintain steady-state capacity with minimal reserve (N_base), add leased GPUs during spike and 2–3 contractors for runbook/burst ops.
- Option B (12–36 mo commit + hire HC): increase committed capacity sufficient for 85% peak; hire 2 FTE infra engineers to run and optimize, reduce contractor hours.

Quick spreadsheet snapshot (monthlyized numbers, simplified):
Columns: Scenario | Base GPUs committed | Additional leased GPUs (avg during month) | Commited cost | Lease cost | HC delta cost | Contractor cost | Expected SLA penalty | Total monthly cost
Rows:
- A (Lease-dominant steady-state): 100 committed | 20 leased | $110,000 | $24,000 | +$0 | $38,880 (3 contractors 160h) | $0 | $172,880
- B1 (12-mo commit + hires): 120 committed | 0 leased | $132,000 | $0 | +$68,000 (2 FTE) | $0 | $0 | $200,000
- B2 (24-mo commit): 120 committed | 0 leased | $114,000 | $0 | +$68,000 | $0 | $0 | $182,000
- B3 (36-mo commit): 120 committed | 0 leased | $98,400 | $0 | +$68,000 | $0 | $0 | $166,400
Notes: committed cost is committed GPUs * per-GPU reserved effective price. Base committed of 100 is current baseline. HC delta cost computed as 2 hires at fully-loaded $34k/mo each. Contractor cost in A assumes 3 contractors covering burst ops and on-call during spike. SLA penalty assumed zero in B rows since committed capacity sized for peak but could be nonzero if demand > estimate.

Sensitivity slices (what changes decision boundary):
1) Spike intensity: if spike is only 2x instead of 4.5x, lease path (A) looks ~18% cheaper monthly vs 12-mo commit. If spike is >5x, commit + hires dominates due to runaway lease/contractor premium and SLA risk.
2) Contractor hourly cost: if contractor rates rise to $160/hr, Option A monthly goes up ~$9.6k — pushes break-even toward commitments.
3) Committed discount erosion: if 12-mo reserved discount slips by 10% (market movement), break-even shifts ~+$11k/mo in committed favor.
4) Diff in utilization: raising steady-state utilization to 70% makes commitments more attractive (committed cost amortized over higher utilization).

Embed small run of Monte-Carlo-ish scenarios (discrete sample):
- Low-demand case (prob 40%): spike magnitude 1.5x; months with extra lease = 10%; Expected monthly cost (A) $150k, (B2) $170k.
- Mid-demand (prob 45%): spike magnitude 2.5x; leases for 25% of month; A $175k, B2 $182k.
- High-demand (prob 15%): spike magnitude 4.5x; leases for 40% of month; A $211k (w/ 2 SLA-risk months factored), B2 $185k.
Expected value (weighted) sample: A ~$171k vs B2 ~$181k -> A lower in base EV but with tail risk (SLA).

Non-financial considerations (must include qualitatively):
- Latency risk and customer experience: leased GPUs often have noisier tail latency and may increase error budget. If priority customers during spike, SLA risk likely to damage GTM.
- Operational burden: contractor-heavy path increases knowledge fragmentation. Committed + FTE builds runbook continuity and optimization potential (quantization/offload) that reduces future per-token cost over 6–9 months.
- Balance-sheet and capex perspective: multi-year commitments show up as operating commitments; may affect covenant metrics vs spot lease which is OPEX.

Recommendation (working):
- Short-term (Q3–Q4 2026): pursue hybrid approach: commit an incremental 10% (move from 100 -> 110 committed GPUs via 12-mo step) to cover predictable baseline growth and hire 1 senior infra engineer (hire now) + 1 contractor standby for spike ops. Continue to lease/spot for remaining peak capacity.
- Medium-term (2027 planning): re-evaluate after 2 quarters of post-hire optimization. If utilization >65% and average monthly lease spend >$18k, accelerate to 24–36 mo commitments and hire second infra engineer.
- Pricing sensitivity guardrails: set automatic thresholds in finance dashboard: if average monthly leased GPU spend > $20k for 2 consecutive months OR contractor spend > $30k -> trigger commit review.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Finance to add real-time leased GPU spend widget to console (owner: Marco Li) — ETA 2026-06-10.
- Recruiting to open SR infra hire req (owner: Diane Park) — pull candidate pipeline by 2026-06-24.
- Infra to produce runbook for burst onboarding and SLA play (owner: Omar El-Sayed) — draft by 2026-06-07.
- Legal to review 12-mo and 24-mo reservation terms for early exit clauses (owner: Nora Chen) — 2026-06-14.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Exact reseller pricing for bulk short-term lease during Aug 2026 — we have quotes but need binding rates.
- Effectiveness of optimization knobs (bespoke quantization + KV cache improvements) in reducing peak GPU need — pilot expected midsummer but uncertain.
- Potential new enterprise customer with committed revenue in July; should influence commit sizing but TBD.

Notes to self / scratch:
- This doc is intentionally conservative w.r.t SLA penalty modeling (flat $45k/mo). Re-run with customer-specific revenue-at-risk mapping once CS provides list of tier-1 customers during spike window.
- Keep this as deck appendix for exec review; main ask = approve 1x 12-mo incremental commit + approve 1 hire.
